headline: CHINA BLOCKS $54B ANGLO-TECK CLOSE: COPPER CONCENTRATE SUPPLY GUARANTEES DEMANDED AS SOLE REMAINING CONDITION
snippet: China's State Administration for Market Regulation has told Anglo American to commit to a steady flow of copper concentrate supply as the sole remaining condition for approving its US$54 billion merger with Teck Resources — a demand that leverages Beijing's effective veto over a deal consolidating roughly 5% of global copper supply. China's copper smelting industry faces its worst feedstock shortage in decades as declining TC/RCs squeeze profitability, and the commitments sought extend to volumes sold through traders. Every other global regulator has cleared the deal; closure is now targeted for March 2027.

headline: ARGENTA SILVER BLASTS 1,599 G/T OVER 4M AT EL QUEVAR STEP-OUT — PLUS NEW 46M GOLD-COPPER TARGET CONFIRMED AT CARMEN
snippet: Argenta Silver (TSX-V: AGAG) extended the El Quevar silver system in Salta, Argentina, with step-out drilling returning 1,599 g/t silver over 4 metres — including 2,780 g/t Ag over 2m at the high-grade core. The program also confirmed a new discovery at the Carmen gold-copper target, with hole QVD-465 returning 0.45 g/t gold and 0.19% copper over 46.0 metres from 233 metres depth, adding a district-scale polymetallic angle to what had been a pure silver play.

headline: TOP 50 MINING COMPANIES SHED $264B IN Q3 AS GOLD TRADE UNWINDS AND LITHIUM STOCKS EXIT THE INDEX
snippet: The world's 50 largest mining companies by market cap gave back $264 billion in Q3 2026 as gold's retreat from its 2026 peak erased most of the sector's earlier gains and lithium miners continued to exit the index despite recovering carbonate prices. Six companies — BHP, Rio Tinto, Agnico Eagle, Zijin Mining, Southern Copper, and Newmont — now hold valuations above $100 billion, while junior and mid-tier miners disproportionately absorbed the sector-wide markdown.

headline: CHINA'S ANTIMONY CLOCK EXPIRES NOV. 27 — DEFENSE BUYERS RACE TO STOCKPILE BEFORE EXPORT BAN COULD RETURN
snippet: China's temporary suspension of antimony export controls expires November 27, 2026, triggering a race among Western defense contractors, industrial users, and tech manufacturers to accumulate inventory before a potential hard re-imposition. China controls 61% of global antimony production; prices remain 170% above 2024 levels as the U.S. Defense Logistics Agency accelerates stockpiling of the metal essential for armor-piercing ammunition, infrared sensors, and flame retardants. Junior miners with non-Chinese antimony assets are attracting renewed attention ahead of the deadline.

headline: VERDE AGRITECH / MAGNES RARE EARTHS: BROAD NdPr-Dy-Tb HITS FROM SURFACE AT MINAS AMERICAS — MAIDEN RESOURCE ADVANCING
snippet: Verde AgriTech's Magnes Rare Earths subsidiary reported broad magnet and heavy rare earth intersections from surface at the Minas Americas ionic clay project in Minas Gerais, Brazil, building on a 443-hole dataset that includes highlights of 15m at 1.15% TREO from surface. With more than 3.6 kilometres of reported assays, a maiden mineral resource estimate is advancing for a project targeting NdPr, Dy, and Tb for non-China EV and defence magnet supply chains.

headline: COPPER NOTCHES THIRD STRAIGHT GAIN AS AI TECH RALLY DRIVES RISK APPETITE FOR BASE METALS
snippet: LME copper rose 0.4% for a third consecutive session on October 6, tracking gains in Asian equities after an AI-led tech rally on Wall Street lifted risk appetite. Structural demand from AI data centres and power grid infrastructure is expected to push copper consumption higher through 2027, providing a demand-side floor even as a strengthening U.S. dollar and ongoing Chile labour negotiations create short-term price headwinds.

headline: F3 URANIUM'S NEW CEO PIVOTS TOWARD BUYOUT: JR DEPOSIT 11.8 MLbs AT 4.39% U3O8 TARGETS AN ACQUIRER
snippet: F3 Uranium Corp.'s new CEO is steering the company toward an M&A exit for its flagship JR deposit in the Patterson Lake North area of Saskatchewan — an 11.8-million-pound inferred resource grading 4.39% U3O8, with a high-grade domain at 12.23%, among the highest early-stage grades in the Athabasca Basin. With $22 million cash in hand and M&A premiums averaging 30–50% in the current uranium consolidation cycle, the strategy positions F3 as a near-term acquisition target for larger Athabasca operators.

headline: GOLD 26% BELOW ITS 2026 PEAK AT $4,168 — BUY THE CORRECTION OR WAIT FOR THE FOMC?
snippet: With gold at $4,168 per ounce — down 26% from its 2026 peak — retail investors face a binary decision ahead of the October 27–28 FOMC meeting: enter now on what could be a generational dip in a structurally bullish market, or wait while the dollar index sits at a 2026 high and 10-year Treasury yields hold near 5.22%. The analysis frames the current correction as less severe than 2011–2012 but warns that weak payrolls data alone is insufficient to break the dollar-led headwind for gold.

headline: GOLDEN MINERALS DRILLS THREE GOLD-COPPER TARGETS AT ARGENTINA'S DESIERTO — 45.8 G/T GOLD IN GRAB SAMPLES AT COBRE
snippet: Golden Minerals Company (TSX: AUMN) commenced a 1,250-metre inaugural drill program at the Desierto property in Argentina on October 6, targeting the Sico, Cobre, and Iceberg gold-copper prospects where surface grab samples at Cobre have returned up to 45.8 g/t gold. The program represents the first systematic drill test of the property, which lies in Argentina's expanding precious metals exploration corridor, with initial assays expected before year-end.

headline: TNM DRILL DOWN: CONTANGO KITSAULT VALLEY LEADS OCTOBER SILVER ASSAYS — 506 G/T AgEq OVER 13.9M AT TORBRIT
snippet: The Northern Miner's weekly drill-results roundup for October 6 named Contango Silver & Gold's (TSX/NYSE-A: CTGO) Kitsault Valley Project in British Columbia — 506 g/t AgEq over 13.9 metres at Torbrit — as the top silver intercept of the past month, alongside Sun Silver (ASX: SS1) and Minaurum Silver (TSXV: MGG) among the leaders. Separate results from Contango's Lucky Shot gold project in Alaska included 2.45m at 86 g/t Au.

headline: GOLD MINERS SHOW UNCHARACTERISTIC DISCIPLINE IN $21B TAKEOVER RUSH — SCRIP OVER CASH, SYNERGIES OVER TROPHIES
snippet: Gold producers completed 32 acquisitions worth a combined $21 billion over the past year — the highest deal value in 15 years — but with unusual discipline: transactions are skewed toward scrip rather than cash, target complementary assets rather than trophy plays, and are sized to avoid triggering 2012-style goodwill write-downs. Gold Fields' hostile all-stock bid for Northern Star is cited as the defining example of a sector that absorbed its past M&A impairment lessons.
